channel.title: Minimal Containers
channel.description: Migration guides and published scan data for free, hardened container images.

item.title: The Redis license field nobody rechecked for nine months
item.description: Our redis-slim build has declared SSPL-1.0 since it was created in January. Redis stopped being SSPL-only in May. The field was correct on day one, which is how it stayed wrong for nine months.

item.title: Why kaniko has 132 CVEs and haproxy has zero, in the same catalog
item.description: 43% of our images scan clean. One of the rest has 132 unique CVEs. Both numbers are honest; the gap is about what the scanner can see, not how carefully either image was built.

item.title: A dependency bump that fixed nothing and broke four builds
item.description: An automated CVE patcher bumped a module nobody had a vulnerability in, and four builds broke the same way. Harmonizing a dependency family's versions is not the same thing as patching one.

item.title: Kafka 4.x moved your config paths and didn't make a fuss about it
item.description: KRaft, Log4j 2, a renamed StorageTool class: Kafka 4.x changed four things upgraders hit blind, because the errors don't mention that a major version happened.

item.title: A red build is usually not your bug
item.description: Most CI failures in a dependency-heavy pipeline are someone else's outage wearing a convincing error message. How to classify one in about two minutes before you start debugging.

item.title: Debugging a container that has no shell
item.description: Distroless images remove the shell an attacker would use, and the one you would use. Here are the techniques that still work, in the order you should reach for them.

item.title: Permission denied: running containers as a non-root user
item.description: Almost every non-root container failure is one of four things. What each looks like, why the fix is not chmod 777, and how to make a directory writable in the image itself.

item.title: Why your scanner reports zero CVEs
item.description: A clean Grype report can mean your image is clean, or it can mean the scanner never identified the software inside it. Here is the difference, and how to tell which one you have.

item.title: Migrating from Minimus to Minimal
item.description: What actually breaks when you move a container image to Minimal: the missing shell, the non-root UID, and the tag you should not have pinned. With the commands to verify what you pulled.
